subject: On-prem VPC BGP sessions & service IP cutover - ACME
messages:
From: ACME Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - BGP peering schedule + service IP handoff (proposal)

Hi Rishi / team,

We are preparing the network change window for the ACME private deployment and want to lock down two items before we schedule the cutover:

1) BGP sessions and ASN exchange – we propose establishing the two iBGP neighbors from the on-prem PE to ACME spine nodes on 10.8.1.0/30 and 10.8.1.4/30.
2) Service IP allocation – attached is our proposed svc-ip-allocation-v1.xlsx with /24 blocks per AZ. We need Redwood to confirm which addresses will host control-plane endpoints (API, auth) vs data-plane service IPs (inference frontends).

Proposed cutover window: Tue, 2027-06-08 02:00-05:00 UTC (low traffic). Please confirm:
- Who will own the route advertisement for the control-plane VIPs after cutover?
- NAT/egress expectations for control-plane -> telemetry endpoints (do you expect us to SNAT at our edge or let your VPC egress?)

Attachments: svc-ip-allocation-v1.xlsx, bgp-session-config.txt

Quick ask: can you +1 the window or propose an alternate by EOD today? We need the change request (CHG-3421) to be complete.

Thanks,
Ellie Park
ACME Cloud Ops

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: ACME Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.com>, SRE Team <sre@acmecloud.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - BGP peering schedule + service IP handoff (proposal)

Thanks Ellie — good detail. We can target the proposed window but need to clarify a couple of points before we sign-off:

- Control-plane vs data-plane separation: Redwood prefers control-plane VIPs be announced by Redwood's control-plane routers for faster failover and tighter ACLs. Data-plane inference frontends may be announced by ACME (your edge) to keep path locality. Can you confirm you can accept that split?

- NAT/Egress: Our telemetry/metrics from control-plane (outbound) must originate from a stable egress IP so customers can whitelist. We can either:
  * Option A: Redwood will SNAT control-plane egress at our VPC NAT (we'll provide single IPs per region), or
  * Option B: ACME will SNAT at their edge and provide the stable IPs.

Jonas: can you validate the firewall ports below are sufficient for the control-plane split? I listed a minimal set.

- Control-plane (recommended): TCP 443 (API), TCP 8443 (internal health), UDP 4750 (metrics/telemetry), 12250-12255 (control sync).
- Data-plane: TCP 80/443 for inference traffic, ephemeral gRPC ports 50051-50060 between nodes.

If ACME confirms the BGP subnets and can accept the control-plane announcement split, we will produce a short canary plan (3-step) and a rollback.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Product Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, ACME Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - BGP peering schedule + service IP handoff (proposal)

Adding some concrete constraints for operations (quoting Ellie below):

> Proposed cutover window: Tue, 2027-06-08 02:00-05:00 UTC (low traffic). Please confirm:
> - Who will own the route advertisement for the control-plane VIPs after cutover?
> - NAT/egress expectations for control-plane -> telemetry endpoints (do you expect us to SNAT at our edge or let your VPC egress?)

Notes / checklist for cutover:
- We'll expect ACME to pre-configure BGP neighbors and ensure TTL/security on the sessions match the examples in bgp-session-config.txt.
- Control-plane VIPs: use the 10.240.x.0/24 block in sheet, assign .10 as primary, .11 as standby. 
- BFD: enable BFD on the control-plane sessions with min rx/tx 50ms and multiplier 3.
- Firewall: allow TCP 443 from ACME spine to Redwood control-plane VIPs; allow UDP 4750 from our telemetry collectors to your ingest.
- Test plan:
  1) Pre-checks (AS paths, localpref, community tags) – performed by ACME.
  2) Announce control-plane VIPs from Redwood in canary AZ (only .10), validate kube-proxy health and admin API responses.
  3) Promote remaining VIPs, monitor 15m, then switch data-plane announcements to your edge.

Runbook link (internal): https://redwood-internal.company/ops/runbooks/private-deploy-egress

I attached a simplified checklist (copied into bgp-session-config.txt) and highlighted the BFD parameters.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: SRE Team <sre@acmecloud.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - BGP peering schedule + service IP handoff (proposal)

Thanks, team — this looks good and we can accept the control-plane announced by Redwood and data-plane by ACME. A few clarifications from the SRE side:

- We'll enable BFD with the params Irene suggested.
- We'll own NAT for data-plane egress; for control-plane egress we'll accept Redwood SNAT. Please provide the control-plane egress IPs by Tue EOD so we can whitelist on our side.
- CHG-3421 updated with proposed schedule and the pre-check checklist: https://acmecloud.atlassian.net/browse/CHG-3421 (we added the BFD and canary steps).

Ellie — attaching the change ticket and our post-cutover verification steps. We also uploaded the validated BGP templates to the ticket.

Attachments: svc-ip-allocation-v1.xlsx (updated), bgp-session-config.txt (validated)

Best,
ACME SRE (on behalf of Ellie)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: SRE Team <sre@acmecloud.com>, ACME Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - BGP peering schedule + service IP handoff (proposal)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and confirmation. Next steps from Redwood:

1) We'll provide two control-plane egress IPs (us-west-2) by Tue EOD: 34.82.199.12 and 34.82.199.13.
2) I'll attach a short canary-plan.md (three step plan):
   - Step 1 (Canary announce): Redwood announces control-plane VIP .10 in AZ-1 only; validate API health and admin endpoints 0/30.
   - Step 2 (Observe 15m): if errors < 0.2% and metrics stable, announce remaining control-plane VIPs and let ACME begin data-plane announcements.
   - Step 3 (Rollback): withdraw Redwood control-plane announcement and fail back to ACME if API error > 1.0% or control-plane RTT > 250ms.
3) We'll request ACME to run the pre-check (AS paths, BFD up, community tags) 30m before the window.

I'll push the canary-plan.md and a one-page rollback note to the shared Drive and update CHG-3421. If anything unexpected pops up, loop me in and we can move to a different window.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Product Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
